To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gene for the human cytokine IL-2 maps to human Chromosome 4 and is closely linked to the gene encoding the IL-2 receptor a chain (CD25).

the gene encoding the human IL-2 receptor beta chain maps to chromosome 22q11, that it is expressed at high levels in the thymus and spleen but not in the bone marrow, and that the gene is closely linked to a gene encoding an IL-2 receptor chain that has a high homology with the IL-2R beta chain.
the rat Nos1 gene is located on Chromosome 12 and that the rat Nos2 gene is located on chromosome 1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of genes encoding the IL-4R, IL-7R and the cytokine, IL-4.
the molecular biology of the immune system.
the genetic basis of the immune system, with particular reference to the role of the major histocompatibility (MHC) complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are no significant differences in the expression patterns of Nos1 in the brain of normal and mutant mice, and the expression pattern of Nos1 in normal and mutant mouse brain is similar to that observed in the human brain.

the NOS1 gene is located on the distal region of the long arm of Chromosome 12 in the mouse, in humans it is located on Chromosome 12q24.23, and in the rat it is located on the short arm of Chromosome l2.
the NOS1 locus has been mapped to rat chromosome 12.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat NOS1 gene is located at the distal part of the rat Chromosome 1.
the gene is mapped to rat Chromosome (Chr) 12, the syntenic region of the human Chr 16, and that the gene is expressed in a variety of tissues, including spleen, thymus, and lymph node.
we identified a gene that was not known before to be involved in the regulation of T-cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a lot of diversity in the way that people think about the immune response and the way that the immune system is regulated, and we need to understand that diversity in order to understand the immune response.
the genetic basis for the variation in the immune response in mice and humans is very similar.
the immune system is not a static entity.
